result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): B wins narrowly because it gives explicit time bands (under 1s, 1–10s, over 10s) plus an indicator delay, which answers 'loading is loading' most directly; A only mentions a quarter-second threshold and otherwise sorts by action. A is better on failure handling (a stated rule that failures stay visible, a persistent download link) and is shorter. B runs longer, and its 'why it's worth doing' section drifts toward a lecture. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers propose sensible treatments for each action, and both cover the export flow well. B handles failure after the screen has moved on more directly ('failures stay visible until the customer notices them', plus save and rename errors), keeps the downloaded file reachable after the toast is gone, and reads more like a collegial message with open questions. A gives clearer explicit time bands, but it is longer and more lecture-like, and it says less about recovering from failed optimistic updates.
